profile.headline: Sarbecovirus subgenus; SARS-CoV caused the 2002–2004 SARS epidemic and SARS-CoV-2 the COVID-19 pandemic.
profile.syndrome: SARS-CoV-2: asymptomatic infection through to severe pneumonia, ARDS, thromboembolic and multi-organ disease, with post-acute sequelae (long COVID). SARS-CoV: severe atypical pneumonia with ~10% case fatality and little pre-symptomatic transmission.
profile.transmission: Respiratory aerosols and droplets; fomite and faecal routes are secondary.
profile.reservoir: Horseshoe bats (Rhinolophus) harbour the closest relatives; intermediate hosts implicated (palm civets for SARS-CoV).
profile.incubation: 2–14 days (median ~3–5 days for recent SARS-CoV-2 variants).
profile.diagnosis: RT-PCR and antigen testing on respiratory specimens; serology for past infection.
profile.management: Antivirals (nirmatrelvir–ritonavir, remdesivir) for those at risk of progression; dexamethasone and IL-6 inhibitors for hypoxaemic disease; oxygen and ventilatory support.
profile.prevention: mRNA and protein-subunit vaccines with periodic variant updates; ventilation, respirators in high-risk settings.
evidence: The most intensively documented emergence of a human pathogen in history, with full genomic, clinical and interventional evidence.
